S54.02.note: The available-plugins part is not a list in the Discover tab; it points to agi marketplace browse. Plugin tab reads installed plugins only.
steps: Start the app, sign in, and type /plugins then Enter.
Look for the title Plugins and the tabs Discover, Installed, Marketplaces, Errors. The overlay opens on Installed.
Press Left or Right to move to Discover. It shows text and commands only, not a list of plugin names.
On Installed, check that each installed plugin appears with a status dot under User or Project.
Compare with Expected: installed plugins are listed; the Discover tab does not list available plugins by name.
S54.02.where: Type /plugins in the chat (opens the Plugins overlay). CLI: agi plugin list

S54.03.note: No customization area or menu was found in the code. Skills are separate slash commands, not a tab beside the Plugins overlay.
steps: Type /skills and press Enter. Look for the list headed Skills with a count, or the message No skills found.
Type /skills-toggle and press Enter to open the overlay titled Skills.
Use the arrow keys to move, Space to toggle a skill, and Enter to save.
Compare with Expected: a Skills section sits beside plugins in the customization area.
S54.03.where: Type /skills in the chat (text list). Type /skills-toggle to open the Skills overlay

S54.04.needs: a paid account (the code gates connectors to paid plans; a refusal message is shown otherwise)
S54.04.note: The connectors output is plain text, not a section in a customization screen.
steps: Sign in, type /connectors and press Enter.
Look for the text Your account's connectors, then the list or None connected yet.
Run agi connectors in a terminal and compare the same heading.
Compare with Expected: a Connectors section is shown.
S54.04.where: Type /connectors in the chat. CLI: agi connectors

labels.text: Add a publisher's marketplace to your account:

S54.05.needs: a signed-in account and a marketplace that the account has added; external service
S54.05.note: The code has no built-in public catalogue. Browse shows only marketplaces added to the account, and the catalogue comes from the server. The owner decision on this item is open.
steps: Add a marketplace first (see S54.07), or run agi marketplace sources to see what the account has.
Run agi marketplace browse and read the plugin list it prints.
Run agi marketplace get <plugin>@<marketplace> on a listed plugin to install it.
Compare with Expected: the user can browse a public marketplace and install from it.

labels.text: Add a publisher's marketplace to your account:

S54.07.needs: a public GitHub repository with a marketplace manifest, and a signed-in account
S54.07.note: The Discover tab says No marketplace yet? Add one from the Marketplaces tab, but that tab shows only the command text, with no add control.
steps: Run agi marketplace add owner/repo with a public GitHub repository that has a marketplace manifest (use --ref for a branch or tag if needed).
Run agi marketplace sources and check that the new marketplace is listed with its plugin count.
Run agi marketplace browse and check that its plugins are listed.
Run agi marketplace get <plugin>@<marketplace> and check that the plugin installs.
S54.07.where: CLI: agi marketplace add <github url>, then agi marketplace sources, agi marketplace browse, agi marketplace get <plugin>@<marketplace>. Hint text is on the Marketplaces tab of /plugins

labels.text: Search the plugin directory: agi marketplace search <query>

S54.08.needs: a signed-in account with marketplaces added; external service
S54.08.note: Search takes only a query. The only filter found in the code is choosing one marketplace in browse; no other filter flags were found.
steps: Run agi marketplace search with a word from a plugin name or description, such as a word you saw in agi marketplace browse.
Check that matching plugins are listed.
Run agi marketplace browse <marketplace id or name> to show only that marketplace's plugins.
Compare with Expected: the user can search and filter the catalogue.
S54.08.where: CLI: agi marketplace search <query>. Narrow by one marketplace with agi marketplace browse <marketplace>

S54.12.note: The marketplace show command does not print a publisher row; only agi plugin info does.
steps: Run agi plugin list and copy an installed plugin's name.
Run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the Publisher row and the Signature row.
Compare with Expected: the publisher's details are shown (the row reads not stated when the manifest gives none).
S54.12.where: CLI: agi plugin list, then agi plugin info <name>

S54.14.needs: a plugin that includes skills; a plugin folder or git URL to install
S54.14.note: The Skills row shows only a count, not the names. Whether a plugin skill runs is not judged here.
steps: Install a plugin that includes skills (see S54.21), then run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the Skills row and its count.
Type /skills in the chat and look for the skill names from the plugin.
Compare with Expected: the plugin shows its skills and they are usable once installed.
S54.14.where: CLI: agi plugin info <name> (row Skills). Then type /skills in the chat

S54.15.needs: a plugin that bundles a remote or local connection; an outside account for remote sign-in
S54.15.note: The info rows show the connections. No separate connected-status check for plugin connections was found.
steps: Install a plugin that bundles connections, then run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the MCP row (name and target) and the Connects row.
For a remote connection, run agi plugin login <name> (see S54.23) and check it signs in.
Compare with Expected: the plugin shows its connectors and they work once installed.
S54.15.where: CLI: agi plugin info <name> (rows MCP and Connects)

S54.16.note: The Agents row shows only a count; names appear in the agent picker.
steps: Install a plugin that includes agents, then run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the Agents row and its count.
Type /agents and press Enter to open the agent picker.
Compare with Expected: the plugin's agents appear and can be used.
S54.16.where: CLI: agi plugin info <name> (row Agents). Then type /agents in the chat

S54.17.note: The Commands row shows only a count. The code did not show where a tester reads the plugin's command names, so find them from the plugin's own files.
steps: Install a plugin that includes commands, then run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the Commands row and its count.
Type a slash command from the plugin in the chat and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the plugin's commands run.
S54.17.where: CLI: agi plugin info <name> (row Commands). Then use a command from the plugin in the chat

S54.18.needs: a plugin that declares hooks, installed from a path or git URL (not inside a project folder)
S54.18.note: Hooks from a project-local plugin are blocked with a stderr warning, so the plugin must be installed for the user, not in a project folder.
steps: Install a plugin that declares hooks, then run agi plugin info <name>.
Look for the Hooks row, which reads runs commands on followed by the event names.
Type /hooks and press Enter to see hook settings.
Compare with Expected: the plugin's hooks are shown and run when installed.
S54.18.where: CLI: agi plugin info <name> (row Hooks). Then type /hooks in the chat

S54.21.needs: a plugin folder or a git URL
S54.21.note: Install is a CLI command only; the chat /plugins view has no install control.
steps: Run agi plugin install with a local plugin folder or a git URL.
Read the line that starts Installed to and the rows printed under it.
Run agi plugin list and check the plugin shows as enabled.
Compare with Expected: the user can install a plugin.
S54.21.where: CLI: agi plugin install <path or git url>. Marketplace plugins: agi marketplace get <plugin>@<marketplace>

labels.text: Sign in to the remote connections an installed plugin bundles.

S54.23.needs: an installed, enabled plugin with a remote connection; an outside account to sign in to
S54.23.note: The command stops with an error if the plugin is turned off. The sign-in text is in the command's help, not in a screen.
steps: Install a plugin that bundles a remote connection, and make sure it is enabled (see S54.24).
Run agi plugin login <name>.
Follow the sign-in step it shows for each remote connection.
Run agi plugin info <name> and check the MCP row, then compare with Expected.

labels.text: Turn an installed plugin off without removing it.

S54.24.note: Enable and disable also work from the chat with /plugins enable or disable followed by the name.
steps: Run agi plugin list and note the plugin shows as enabled.
Run agi plugin disable <name> and read the message it prints.
Run agi plugin list and check the plugin shows as disabled, and that it is still listed.
Run agi plugin enable <name> and check it shows as enabled again.
S54.24.where: CLI: agi plugin disable <name> and agi plugin enable <name>. Chat: /plugins disable <name> and /plugins enable <name>

labels.text: Update a plugin installed from git to its latest commit.

S54.25.needs: a plugin installed from a git URL and a newer commit in that repository
S54.25.note: Update works only for plugins installed from git. Plugins installed from a path have no update source.
steps: Install a plugin from a git URL, then push a newer commit to that repository.
Run agi plugin update <name> and read the line it prints.
Run agi plugin info <name> and check the Version row.
Compare with Expected: the plugin moves to the newer version.
S54.25.where: CLI: agi plugin update <name> (plugins installed from git). All marketplace plugins: agi marketplace update

labels.text: install it again with --ref <tag> to move it

S54.26.needs: a git plugin repository with a tag and a newer commit
S54.26.note: The pin is set with the --ref flag on install; no separate pin command was found.
steps: Install a git plugin with --ref set to a tag, for example agi plugin install <git url> --ref v1.0.0.
Run agi plugin update <name> and read the message.
Check that the message says the plugin is pinned to that tag.
Compare with Expected: the plugin stays on the pinned version.
S54.26.where: CLI: agi plugin install <git url> --ref <TAG_OR_BRANCH>, then agi plugin update <name>

S54.29.needs: an installed plugin you can afford to remove
S54.29.note: The remove command has no confirmation prompt in the code; it removes the plugin right away.
steps: Run agi plugin list and note the plugin name.
Run agi plugin remove <name> and read the line it prints.
Run agi plugin list and check the plugin is gone.
Compare with Expected: the user can uninstall the plugin.
S54.29.where: CLI: agi plugin remove <name>. Marketplace plugins: agi marketplace uninstall <name>. Chat: /plugins remove <name>

S54.33.needs: a plugin with a version range this CLI does not meet
S54.33.note: The check covers only the engines.agiworkforce version range. No check for the surface the plugin runs on was found, so the surface half of Expected is not in the code.
steps: Install a plugin whose manifest sets an engines.agiworkforce version range that this CLI version does not meet.
Type /plugins and press Right until the Errors tab, or type /plugins Errors.
Look for a line that reads plugin requires agiworkforce and the range, with this CLI's version.
Compare with Expected: the product warns that the plugin is not compatible.
S54.33.where: Chat: /plugins, then the Errors tab (or type /plugins Errors)
